samples.summary: `unwrapJson`'s new `catch { detachYorkieValue(value) }` fallback silently changes behaviour for its four pre-existing callers, three of which document that `detachYorkieValue` returns WRONG data for their shapes
samples.evidence:
The diff changes `unwrapJson` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:21-25) from `JSON.parse(str)` (throws on failure) to `parseJsonSnapshot(str)` with a fallback to `detachYorkieValue(value)`. Out-of-diff consumers that never asked for that fallback:
- packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-charts.controller.ts:62-71 — its own comment states: "`unwrapJson`, never a spread and never `detachYorkieValue` … `detachYorkieValue` does not save it either — it branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for an array proxy, so the array comes back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata." With the new fallback, a chart whose repaired parse still fails is now returned to the caller as chart metadata garbage (`seriesColumns: {createdAt, movedAt}`) with HTTP 200, instead of the previous loud 500.
- packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:69-75 and 117-121 make the identical argument ("`unwrapJson`, not `detachYorkieValue`") and are now silently downgraded the same way.
- packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:64-68 unwraps `themes/masters/layouts/slides/guides` array proxies — exactly the `Array.isArray`-false case — so a parse failure now yields CRDT-metadata objects where a deck was expected, which then flows into `readSlidesRoot` consumers including the new `slide-ops` writers.
The fallback is only needed by the new `tabs.duplicate` path; scoping it there (or to a separate helper) would leave the existing readers' documented contract intact.

samples.summary: Backend-authored notifications send the raw comment body as `preview`, so mention tokens reach the notification reader unflattened — unlike every notification the frontend reports
samples.evidence: `planCommentNotifications` in the new controller sets `preview: comment.body` / `preview: thread.comments[0]?.body ?? ''` verbatim. The frontend implementation it claims to mirror does not: packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:35-37 wraps every preview in `preview()` = `mentionBodyToPlainText(body).slice(0, 200)`, which rewrites `@[username](7)` to `@username` (packages/frontend/src/components/comments/mentions.ts:124-130). The shared sink does not compensate: `sanitizePreview` (packages/backend/src/notification/notification.service.ts:67-82) only strips control/bidi characters, collapses whitespace and truncates — it does not touch mention tokens. So an agent-authored mention shows up in the notification dropdown as the literal `look at this @[peer](9)` while the same comment typed in the editor shows `look at this @peer`.

samples.summary: `duplicateTab` copies only three of `TabMeta`'s six optional fields, so the copy silently loses `lakehouseSourceId`, `lakehouseRef` and `asOf`
samples.evidence: `duplicateTab` carries `kind`, `datasourceId` and `query` only. `TabMeta` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:121-131) also has `lakehouseSourceId`, `lakehouseRef` and `asOf`, all of which the frontend writes (packages/frontend/src/app/documents/lakehouse-tab.ts:23-29, and the time-travel `asOf` set from datasource-view). A tab meta copied without them keeps `type` but points at nothing. Today this is largely masked because lakehouse/datasource tabs get no `root.sheets` entry (packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:398-423) and the controller refuses a tab with no worksheet — which also makes the `datasourceId`/`query` copy dead code, so the field list is already inconsistent with itself and will mislead the next edit.

samples.summary: The new writers create the `comments` container lazily, the pattern the sheets model explicitly documents as losing a whole thread under concurrency
samples.evidence: `if (!ws.comments) ws.comments = {}` (sheet path) and `if (!root.comments) root.comments = {}` (pdf path). packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:158-165 seeds `comments: {}` at worksheet creation precisely so this is never done: "If the map were instead created lazily on first comment (`if (!ws.comments) ws.comments = {}`), two users adding the first comment concurrently would each create a fresh map and one — with its thread — would be dropped wholesale." Graded a nit because the frontend keeps the same guard for legacy documents and calls the window acceptable (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts:176-179), so the backend is consistent with existing practice rather than newly unsafe.

samples.summary: CLI re-declares `SheetImage` instead of importing the canonical type, and with a looser shape than the server stores
samples.evidence: http-client.ts:127-140 declares its own `SheetImage` with `originalWidth?`/`originalHeight?` optional. The canonical type is exported from `@wafflebase/sheets` (packages/sheets/src/index.ts:200, 443) with both required, and the server always fills them (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-images.ts defaults them to the placed size). The CLI already depends on the workspace packages for other model types, so this copy is pure drift surface: a future field added to `SheetImage` will type-check in sheets and backend and be silently absent here.

verdict.reason: The described code is present exactly as claimed and the affected consumers are real and unguarded. `unwrapJson` (yorkie-json.ts:14-30) now returns `detachYorkieValue(value)` from a bare `catch` for every caller, and `detachYorkieValue` (yorkie-json.ts:168-181) branches on `Array.isArray` before falling through to `Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(...))`, so a Yorkie array proxy degrades to a metadata object rather than an array — the exact failure mode three out-of-diff callers document as unacceptable for their shapes: worksheet-charts.controller.ts:62-72, worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:69-75 and :117-121, and slides-tree.ts:64-68. The fallback is live, not dead: yorkie-json.spec.ts:155-158 asserts it. Impact is not limited to read responses — readSlidesRoot's output is consumed at slides.controller.ts:174 and the derived change is written back at slides.controller.ts:186-191, so a degraded deck can reach a mutation. No guard, validation, or shape check sits between unwrapJson and any of these consumers, so `already-guarded` does not apply; a behaviour change to a shared exported symbol whose other consumers were not updated is squarely in the blast-radius lane, so `out-of-scope` does not apply either. The site that changes behaviour silently (200 with wrong shape where the contract-documenting callers previously got a loud failure) is a caller-visible contract regression: major.
